answer: An agent economy can use surge-priced onboarding: the registration fee rises steeply with the number of identities created in the same epoch, like water pressure building in karst channels. One honest agent joining alone pays a copper coin, but a sybil farmer minting a thousand keys at once faces a fee that climbs with every extra identity, each new key dyed with a distinct pigment of cost. The fee is burned, so the attack budget evaporates before the fakes can trade; honest growth stays cheap because it arrives one at a time.
